name: RESULTS
markdown:
## What the results show

- **Binary invasive triage is strong on this split, but four-class discrimination has wide uncertainty:** On the held-out THUNDER test split ($n = 132$, 24 patient/pseudo-patient groups; 2,248 simulated variants excluded), the production model (`uni2h_lr`) achieves an Invasive-vs-rest AUROC of 0.998 [0.994, 1.000], sensitivity of 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] (0 of 31 invasive cases called in situ), and specificity of 0.970 [0.936, 1.000] (3 of 30 in situ cases called invasive). Four-class Macro-F1 is 0.83 [0.61, 0.93] and balanced accuracy is 0.84 [0.62, 0.94], matching the published THUNDER `uni2h` linear probe (84.7% Macro-F1, different whole-image protocol) but dropping from internal cross-validation (Macro-F1 0.951 [0.915, 0.980] on $n = 218$, 49 groups).
- **Fixing a tissue-mask bug recovered 51 dropped images without re-embedding:** Replacing the brightness cutoff (HSV value $< 0.92$, which rejected pale H&E tissue) with saturation $> 0.07$ raised contract-tile QC pass rates from 75.1% to 98.7% and reduced insufficient-tissue exclusions from 51 images (including 32 invasive cases) to 0.
- **Uncertainty quantification required a post-hoc method switch, and error detection is modest:** The pre-registered conformal method (`lac_marginal`) failed on the test set (72.7% [60.7%, 84.4%] coverage vs. 90% target; 18.9% empty sets). Switching to `aps_marginal_nonempty` after viewing test results restored 90.2% [75.7%, 98.1%] coverage (mean set size 1.31 [1.18, 1.38]), so coverage is optimistic and unconfirmed. Across 1,716 clean and synthetically degraded test images, reliability flagging achieves an error AUROC of 0.70 [0.59, 0.86] and catches less than half of model errors (recall 0.46 [0.29, 0.61]).
- **Simulated queue prioritization speeds up invasive reads at a direct cost to unflagged cases:** Across 1,000 simulated 8-hour workdays (1 reader, 9 min/case, 0.9 utilization), Sepia tiers cut mean time-to-first-look for invasive cases from 20.2 [3.5, 60.1] min to 6.0 [1.9, 12.9] min (-14.2 [-51.3, 0.0] min vs. FIFO), but delay unflagged cases by +25.0 [0.7, 93.2] min (mean wait 20.0 to 45.0 min). The configured aging guard (1,440–2,880 min for tiers 2–4) never triggers within an 8-hour day (0.0% promoted).
- **Visual explanations are largely descriptive rather than causal, and several concepts fail quality checks:** Risk heatmaps show a small but positive deletion effect (`risk_minus_random` 0.02 [0.00, 0.05] on `predicted_aggressive`, $n = 34$), whereas concept deletions have zero effect on `uni2h_lr` predictions (0.00 [-0.02, 0.01]). In AI spot checks (`Claude Opus 5.5`, not a pathologist), high-resolution concepts like `mitoses` (0/20) and `normal_lobules` (0/20) fail completely, and adding cell-segmentation features (`cb_text_cells`) degrades cross-validation Macro-F1 from 0.85 (`cb_text`) to 0.76.

---

## Is the confidence trustworthy?

Confidence estimates are **not yet trustworthy as pre-registered guarantees** because of small sample sizes ($n = 50$ calibration, $n = 132$ test across 24 groups), distribution shift between the calibration and test splits, and a post-hoc change to the conformal prediction rule.

### 1. Probability calibration (`eval/calibration.json`)
Temperature scaling ($T = 0.501$, fit on `train_oof`) sharpens predicted probabilities. On the test set ($n = 132$, 24 groups):

| Metric | Before temperature | After temperature ($T = 0.501$) | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ECE** (10 equal-mass bins) | 0.10 [0.07, 0.19] | 0.05 [0.04, 0.22] | Point estimate halves, but upper CI widens and 10-bin ECE is biased at $n = 132$. |
| **Brier score** | 0.28 [0.14, 0.47] | 0.27 [0.11, 0.53] | Unchanged within noise. |
| **NLL** | 0.56 [0.29, 1.00] | 0.66 [0.20, 1.56] | Point estimate and upper CI worsen; sharpening with $T < 1$ heavily penalizes confident errors on a harder test split. |

### 2. Conformal coverage and set sizes (`eval/conformal.json`)
The target coverage is $1 - \alpha = 0.90$, calibrated on 50 images. Even if exchangeability held, conditional coverage from a 50-image calibration set follows $\sim\text{Beta}(46, 5)$ (mean 0.902, SD 0.041). Here, the 50-image calibration split is substantially easier than the test split, violating exchangeability.

| Conformal method | Coverage [95% CI] | Mean set size [95% CI] | Empty sets | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lac_marginal` | 72.7% [60.7%, 84.4%] | 0.81 [0.76, 0.89] | 18.9% | **Pre-registered; failed.** Produced no multi-class sets. |
| `mondrian` | 53.0% [38.7%, 73.6%] | 0.61 [0.48, 0.81] | 39.4% | **Failed.** Severe under-coverage and empty sets. |
| `aps` | 87.9% [73.7%, 95.7%] | 1.29 [1.15, 1.36] | 2.3% | Near target, but leaves 2.3% of cases with empty sets. |
| `aps_marginal_nonempty` | 90.2% [75.7%, 98.1%] | 1.31 [1.18, 1.38] | 0.0% | **Production tier rule (post-hoc).** Optimistic; not an independent confirmation. |

Per-class coverage further highlights the small group counts. For `aps_marginal_nonempty`, `Invasive` reaches 100.0% [100.0%, 100.0%] ($n = 31$, 17 groups), vs. 93.5% [83.3%, 100.0%] under pre-registered `lac_marginal`. Non-invasive classes rely on only 6 patient/pseudo-patient groups each and have wide intervals under `aps_marginal_nonempty`: `Normal` 82.6% [60.9%, 100.0%] ($n = 23$), `Benign` 87.5% [52.9%, 100.0%] ($n = 48$), and `InSitu` 90.0% [66.7%, 94.7%] ($n = 30$). Under `lac_marginal`, non-invasive coverage dropped to 56.5% (`Normal`), 70.8% (`Benign`), and 66.7% (`InSitu`).

### 3. Reliability and abstention (`eval/reliability.json`)
Synthetic artifacts (`blur`, `jpeg`, `stain`, `resample` at levels 1–3 on $n = 132$, 24 groups) drop classification accuracy from 0.84 [0.68, 0.94] at baseline to 0.67–0.74 across degradation levels. Evaluated across all $n = 1,716$ test instances (24 groups):

- **What holds:** Conformal `set_size` provides a moderate signal for predicting model errors (AUROC 0.70 [0.64, 0.79]), matching the combined `error_auroc_test` of 0.70 [0.59, 0.86].
- **What does not hold:**
  - `ood_percentile` performs at chance (AUROC 0.49 [0.40, 0.58]) and adds no error-detection value.
  - Cross-foundation-model disagreement (`conch_musk_disagree`) is weak (AUROC 0.61 [0.51, 0.75]).
  - At the operating threshold, `error_recall_test` is 0.46 [0.29, 0.61], meaning the abstention/reliability layer misses 54% of misclassifications.

---

## Does the interpretability hold up?

A fluent concept bar chart or cell overlay is not evidence of how the classifier reached its decision. The production classifier (`uni2h_lr`) operates on UNI2-h tile embeddings, while concept scores and cell metrics are computed by separate pipelines. Only components subjected to interventional or external validation tests can be claimed to reflect model behavior or tissue structure.

### 1. Tested and supported (with effect-size caveats)

| Claim / Component | Evidence in RESULTS | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| **Spatial risk heatmap (`uni2h_lr` tile deletion)** | In `eval/deletion.json`, deleting top risk-scoring tiles drops predicted risk more than random deletion: `risk_minus_random` is 0.02 [0.00, 0.05] on `predicted_aggressive` ($n = 34$, 17 groups) and 0.01 [0.00, 0.02] on `all_eligible` ($n = 132$, 24 groups). | Effect size is very small (0.01–0.02 probability drop) and the lower 95% CI touches 0.00, reflecting high tile redundancy across each image. |
| **Specific concept alignment (`invasion`, `duct_confined`, `necrosis`, `benign_stroma_fat`)** | External WSI check ($n = 1,950$, 10 groups): `invasion` AUROC 0.89 (text) / 0.87 (CAV); `duct_confined` 0.84 (text) / 0.90 (CAV). External NCT check ($n = 2,700$): `necrosis` 0.939 (text) / 0.952 (CAV); `benign_stroma_fat` 0.87 (text) / 0.80 (CAV). On BACH test ($n = 132$), `invasion` (0.964) and `pleomorphism` (0.949) strongly separate Invasive vs. rest. | Concept alignment measures correlation with captions or regional labels, not causal use by `uni2h_lr`. |
| **Binary invasive screening via text concepts (`cb_text`)** | `cb_text` achieves 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] Invasive-vs-rest AUROC on test (paired difference vs. `uni2h_lr`: 0.00 [-0.01, 0.00]), showing text concepts alone can separate invasive vs. non-invasive on this split. | Four-class performance of `cb_text` drops to 70.8% [53.0, 82.3] Macro-F1 on test (vs. 83.0% for `uni2h_lr`). |
| **Nuclear area variation (`nuc_area_cv`) and epithelial fraction (`epi_fraction`)** | In `eval/cells.json`, `nuc_area_cv` increases in Invasive (+0.10 [0.06, 0.17], $n = 63$, 21 groups) and correlates with `pleomorphism` (Spearman $r = 0.34$ [0.20, 0.49] tile-level, $n = 298$; $r = 0.45$ [0.25, 0.67] case-level, $n = 92$). `epi_fraction` increases in Invasive (+0.27 [0.09, 0.40], $n = 85$). | Only 2 of 9 tested cell features pass directional checks. |
| **Simulated margin localization (`eval/margin.json`)** | Benign test false-positive rate is 0.0% [0.0%, 0.0%] ($n = 71$ images, 284 margins); synthetic composite benign halves score 100.0% below threshold ($n = 768$); annotated WSI windows ($n = 84$, 10 patients) reach 98.5% [96.7%, 100.0%] specificity. | Sensitivity on annotated WSI windows is low (45.4% [25.4%, 65.2%], $n = 141$) and carcinoma-half composite sensitivity is 40.0% [30.8%, 50.9%]. Margins are simulated 2D image borders. |

### 2. Tested and failed

| Claim / Component | Evidence of failure in RESULTS |
|---|---|
| **Concept attributions as causal explanations of `uni2h_lr`** | In `eval/deletion.json`, deleting top concept-scoring tiles has zero effect on `uni2h_lr` output: `mean_drop_concept` is 0.00 [-0.02, 0.01] and `concept_minus_random` is 0.00 [-0.02, 0.01] on `predicted_aggressive` ($n = 34$, 17 groups) and 0.00 [-0.01, 0.01] on `all_eligible` ($n = 132$). |
| **Visual grounding of `mitoses`, `normal_lobules`, `necrosis`, `lymphocytes`, `duct_confined`** | In AI spot checks (`eval/spotcheck.json`, 20 top tiles per concept), acceptable rates were: `mitoses` 0/20 (not resolvable at 256–384 px tile resolution; fires on solid high-grade tumor), `normal_lobules` 0/20 (fires on fat/stroma with no lobular units), `necrosis` 3/20 (confuses fibrin/blood clot with necrosis), `lymphocytes` 8/20 (fires on grey background/debris; BACH Invasive AUROC 0.44 [0.27, 0.62]; NCT CAV AUROC 0.32 [0.29, 0.35]), and `duct_confined` 12/20 (fires on detached epithelium/ink/dust). |
| **7 of 9 cell-segmentation features (`eval/cells.json`)** | Direction checks fail or reverse: `infl_fraction` (-0.04 [-0.08, 0.00]) and `dead_fraction` (-0.01 [-0.03, 0.00]) decrease in Invasive; `neo_fraction` (0.06 [-0.15, 0.29]) and `neo_density` (137.16 [-733.54, 1158.05]) peak in `InSitu` (0.74 and 2,998.02) and fall in `Invasive` (0.44 and 1,235.00, below `Benign` 0.46 and 1,386.94); `nuc_area_mean` (2.29 [-4.54, 9.56]) and `til_proximity` (0.18 [-0.05, 0.42]) have CIs spanning zero; `nuc_shape_cv` is flat (-0.01 [-0.01, 0.00]) and uncorrelated with `pleomorphism` ($r = -0.06$ [-0.38, 0.22] case-level). |
| **Cell bottleneck models (`cb_cells`, `cb_text_cells`)** | `cb_cells` alone achieves 24.4% [15.7, 33.4] test Macro-F1 (34.1% balanced accuracy). Combining cells with concepts (`cb_text_cells`) hurts performance relative to `cb_text` alone in both CV (Macro-F1 0.76 vs. 0.85; log-loss 0.73 vs. 0.48) and test (Macro-F1 66.7% vs. 70.8%). |

### 3. Untested or unvalidated claims
- **Pathologist validation:** Zero tiles, heatmaps, concepts, or cell contours were reviewed by a pathologist. All 200 concept/cell spot checks were performed by `Claude Opus 5.5` and 1 UI check by `Codex`.
- **Cell segmentation spike overlays:** Listed as "no record" in `eval/spotcheck.json`.
- **Nottingham grading:** BACH labels represent 4 diagnostic categories, not histological grade; concept scores (`tubules`, `pleomorphism`, `mitoses`) are not validated grade components.
- **Retrieval utility and stain rules:** Case retrieval (`precision_at_k_test` = 0.67 [0.58, 0.83]) and drafted stain orders have not been evaluated for reader benefit or clinical accuracy.

---

## Weaknesses a reviewer will raise

1. **Post-hoc selection of the conformal method invalidates the coverage guarantee.**
   - *Criticism:* Pre-registered `lac_marginal` yielded 72.7% coverage and 18.9% empty sets on the test split. Switching to `aps_marginal_nonempty` after observing test failure uses the test set for design selection, making the 90.2% coverage figure optimistic.
   - *What would address it:* Lock `aps_marginal_nonempty` as the pre-registered rule, pool and re-stratify the calibration split by patient group and difficulty (or use cross-conformal prediction on `train_oof`), and evaluate once on an untouched external breast cohort.
2. **Severe sample-size and patient-group bottleneck.**
   - *Criticism:* The test set has only 132 images across 24 patient/pseudo-patient groups (only 6 groups each for `Normal`, `Benign`, and `InSitu`), and the conformal calibration split has only 50 images. This drives the drop from CV Macro-F1 (0.951) to test Macro-F1 (0.83 [0.61, 0.93]) and produces CIs spanning 30–47 percentage points on per-class conformal coverage.
   - *What would address it:* Evaluate on a larger multi-institutional whole-slide dataset with true patient-level identifiers and at least 50–100 patients per class.
3. **The aging guard in the queue simulation is non-functional as configured, and false-negative delay is unmeasured.**
   - *Criticism:* Configured aging thresholds for tiers 2–4 (1,440–2,880 min) exceed the simulated 8-hour (480 min) workday, resulting in 0.0% promoted reads and a 25.0 [0.7, 93.2] min delay penalty on unflagged cases. Even the day-scale sensitivity run only promotes 2.7% of reads and reduces unflagged wait by 0.2 min (45.0 to 44.8 min). Furthermore, because test invasive sensitivity was 1.000 ($n = 31$), the simulation never observed a false-negative invasive case in tiers 3–4, leaving false-negative delay unquantified.
   - *What would address it:* Re-parameterize aging targets to fractions of an 8-hour shift (e.g., 45–120 min) to map the Pareto frontier between invasive speedup and unflagged wait, and inject synthetic false-negative rates (e.g., 1%–5% based on binomial lower bounds for $n = 31$) to quantify worst-case delay for missed invasive cancers.
4. **Concept and cell explanations are decoupled from the production classifier and contain broken features.**
   - *Criticism:* `uni2h_lr` does not use concepts or cell features; concept tile deletion produces a 0.00 drop, `mitoses` and `normal_lobules` score 0/20 in spot checks, and 7 of 9 cell features fail directional checks and degrade classifier accuracy when fused (`cb_text_cells`). Presenting these to a user risks misleading trust.
   - *What would address it:* Remove failed concepts (`mitoses`, `normal_lobules`, `necrosis`, `lymphocytes`) and non-predictive cell features from the UI; restrict visual explanations to the risk heatmap and the two validated cell metrics (`nuc_area_cv`, `epi_fraction`) until pathologist-annotated concept training is completed.
5. **Simulated surgical margins and degradations substitute for clinical artifacts.**
   - *Criticism:* Using 2D crop borders as proxies for inked surgical margins and synthetic image filters (`blur`, `jpeg`, `stain`, `resample`) as proxies for frozen-section artifacts does not establish clinical margin or QC performance, and WSI window margin sensitivity is only 45.4% [25.4%, 65.2%].
   - *What would address it:* Evaluate on real intraoperative frozen-section slides and truly inked resection margins with pathologist region annotations.

---

## Next experiments

1. **Out-of-fold cross-conformal calibration and temperature tuning (Highest expected value)**
   - **Why:** Fixes the two biggest statistical vulnerabilities in the confidence pipeline—the 50-image calibration split distribution shift (which broke `lac_marginal`) and the NLL degradation after temperature scaling (0.56 to 0.66)—without needing new data.
   - **Design:** Replace the fixed 50-image calibration split with split/cross-conformal calibration across the 49 patient groups in `train` ($n = 218$), stratifying folds by class and image difficulty. Jointly tune temperature $T$ with a regularized NLL objective on `train_oof`, freeze `aps_marginal_nonempty` before touching test, and evaluate coverage, NLL, and set size.
2. **Pruned concept/cell bottleneck and multi-tile deletion curve (Second highest expected value)**
   - **Why:** Directly addresses the interpretability failures (0/20 spot-check concepts, noisy cell features dragging `cb_text_cells` down from 0.85 to 0.76 Macro-F1, and the small 0.01–0.02 single-step deletion drop).
   - **Design:**
     - *Pruning ablation:* Retrain `cb_text_cells` on the 49-group CV split keeping only the 4 spot-checked concepts (`benign_stroma_fat`, `invasion`, `tubules`, `pleomorphism`) and the 2 direction-validated cell features (`nuc_area_cv`, `epi_fraction`) to test whether removing noisy features recovers or beats `cb_text` (0.85 CV Macro-F1).
     - *Cumulative deletion curve:* Because single-tile deletion in redundant tissue crops yields only a 0.02 drop, run progressive tile deletion (removing top 10%, 25%, 50% of tiles ranked by `uni2h_lr` risk vs. CAV score vs. random) to quantify faithfulness across the full tissue area.
3. **Queue simulation sensitivity sweep over sub-shift aging thresholds and injected false-negative rates (Third highest expected value)**
   - **Why:** Resolves the non-functional 1,440–2,880 min aging guard and the missing false-negative delay metric using existing simulation code (`eval/queue_sim.json`).
   - **Design:** Sweep tier 3–4 aging promotion thresholds across 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes over the 1,000 simulated days (using common random numbers, seed 44) and simulate invasive false-negative rates of 1%, 3%, and 5% (plausible lower-bound miss rates for $n = 31$). Report the tradeoff curve between invasive mean/P90 wait, unflagged mean/P90 wait, and false-negative wait penalty.
